To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed and implemented methods to correct for the GC and repeat content biases in the sequencing of cell-free DNA from plasma and that this improves the sensitivity and specificity of the detection of fetal aneuploidies.
we have improved the sensitivity of fetal trisomys detection by correcting for coverage bias in the sequencing data.

1) we have identified and corrected a coverage bias in plasma sequencing that affects detection of aneuploidy; and 2) we have identified a bias in the fragmentation of plasma DNA and developed a correction model for it.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the sensitivity and specificity of non-invasive prenatal testing by correcting for sequencing bias.
improving the sensitivity of fetal trisomie detection in maternal plasma DNA.
improving the detection of fetal aneuploidies and other copy number variation from cell-free DNA sequencing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have shown improvements in the analysis of the plasma sequencing data by reducing the GC bias and better understanding the fragmentation bias, but we have not yet found any way to improve the detection of fetal aneuploidies.
the GC bias is the major cause of the coverage bias, and it can be corrected using the methods described in this paper.
we have shown how to improve the sensitivity of trisomy 12 and 21 detection by reducing the coverage bias.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that we can improve the detection of fetal aneuploidies by improving the coverage bias in plasma DNA sequencing.
we have improved the sensitivity of fetal trisomia detection by 2-3% and have shown that the GC bias and repeat content can be corrected for.

the current state of the art in the field of non-invasive prenatal diagnosis is to perform a targeted enrichment of a set of regions of interest and then to sequence the DNA on a Next-Generation Sequencer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it should be feasible to detect fetal trismories from maternal plasma with a single cell free DNA sample, without the need to collect additional samples for technical replication.
the GC and fragmentation bias in plasma DNA sequencing data are not the main limiting factors for the detection of aneuploidies, although they are important for sub-chromosomal CNV detection.

the current state-of-the-art in fetal trisomy analysis is very sensitive to the sequencing data and its processing, and that the current tests should be improved by incorporating more sophisticated statistical models.
